# Paths across tolerances and outlier-fragility {#tolerance-path}

The CE-FDH ceiling of Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) sets the bottleneck at each outcome target to the lowest condition value among the cases that reach the target, so one case holds each strict bottleneck [@Dul2016]. One valid but unusual efficient case, with a high outcome and a low condition, can lower several bottlenecks and shrink the empty-zone effect size [@Deja2026QNCA]. The ceiling is the strictest boundary that every observed case respects, so one case suffices to move the ceiling [@Deja2026QNCA].

Quantile Necessary Condition Analysis (QNCA) indexes the frontier by a tolerance `pi` in (0, 1], which fixes the share `1 - pi` of successful cases that may sit below the requirement [@Deja2026QNCA]. At a target $y_j$ of the outcome grid, $k_j$ cases reach $Y \ge y_j$, and the raw frontier returns the condition value of rank $h_j = \max\{1, \lceil k_j (1 - \pi) \rceil\}$ among the $k_j$ cases. The monotone envelope takes the running maximum over the lower targets, and the fixed scope sets the requirement to the upper condition bound above the largest observed outcome. The effect size `d_pi` divides the area left of the fitted frontier by the area of the scope rectangle.

## Resistance to added cases

The resistance proposition of @Deja2026QNCA bounds the effect of $c$ cases added at arbitrary positions in the scope. At a target with $h_j > c$, the raw requirement of the augmented sample lies at or above the $(h_j - c)$th smallest condition value of the original successful cases, and at or below the $(h_j + c)$th smallest value whenever $h_j + c \le k_j$. The envelope carries the lower bound to every higher target. The condition $h_j > c$ reads $k_j > c/(1 - \pi)$, so at `pi = 0.95` one added case is absorbed wherever more than 20 original cases reach the target. At `pi = 1`, the rank is 1 at every target, and one added case can lower every bottleneck the added case attains to the condition value of the added case.

## The tolerance path

At a grid target $y_j$, the pointwise gap is $g_\pi(y_j) = \tilde\varphi_\pi(y_j) - \tilde\varphi_1(y_j)$, and the effect-size gap is $g_d(\pi) = d_\pi - d_1$ [@Deja2026QNCA]. Both gaps are zero at `pi = 1` and non-negative at `pi < 1`, because a lower tolerance selects an order statistic of equal or higher rank at every target. A positive pointwise gap identifies a target whose CE-FDH bottleneck rests on the most efficient successful cases.

A flat path over tolerances fixed in advance suggests limited dependence on the cases with the lowest condition values, and a steep path flags outlier-fragility at the affected targets [@Deja2026QNCA]. The pointwise path is the primary display, because decisions concern particular targets and the area gap can be small when a large local change covers a narrow range of targets. The diagnostic sets no pass-or-fail cut-off; the path shows which outcome targets depend on exceptional observed successes [@Deja2026QNCA].

## A clean and a planted sample

The synthetic dataset of 500 cases of the `qnca` repository has a condition and an outcome on a scale from 0 to 100, and the analysis fixes the scope at [0, 100] x [0, 100]. The planted sample adds one efficient case at (X, Y) = (2, 95). The path runs over the tolerances 1.00, 0.99, ..., 0.90, rounded to two decimals because the package reads a tolerance as a decimal with at most nine places.

```{r tolerance-path-path}
library(qnca)
d <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarekDejaUJ/qnca/main/data/qnca_dataset_n500.csv")
scope <- c(0, 100, 0, 100)
planted <- rbind(d, data.frame(X = 2, Y = 95))
pis <- round(seq(1, 0.90, by = -0.01), 2)
d_clean <- sapply(pis, function(p) qnca(d$X, d$Y, pi = p, B = 0, scope = scope)$d_pi)
d_planted <- sapply(pis, function(p) {
  qnca(planted$X, planted$Y, pi = p, B = 0, scope = scope)$d_pi
})
path <- data.frame(pi = pis, d_clean, gap_clean = d_clean - d_clean[1],
                   d_planted, gap_planted = d_planted - d_planted[1])
round(path, 3)
```

On the clean sample, `d_pi` rises from 0.452 at `pi = 1` to 0.558 at `pi = 0.90`, and the gap at `pi = 0.95` is 0.058. The planted case lowers the strict effect size to 0.066 and the effect size at `pi = 0.95` to 0.439, and the gap at `pi = 0.95` widens to 0.373. The planted path is steep at the first steps, with the effect size rising from 0.066 at `pi = 1` to 0.324 at `pi = 0.98`.

```{r tolerance-path-frontiers, fig.cap = "The 500 cases of the synthetic dataset (grey dots) with one planted efficient case at (2, 95) (triangle), fixed scope [0, 100] x [0, 100], grid of 50 outcome targets. The fitted frontier at pi = 1.00 falls to the condition value of the planted case, or lower, at every target the planted case attains; the fitted frontier at pi = 0.95 holds the requirement of the target 67.35, the last target reached by more than 20 cases, up to the outcome 95 of the planted case."}
frontiers <- rbind(
  data.frame(tolerance = "pi = 1.00",
             qnca(planted$X, planted$Y, pi = 1, B = 0, scope = scope)$bottleneck),
  data.frame(tolerance = "pi = 0.95",
             qnca(planted$X, planted$Y, pi = 0.95, B = 0, scope = scope)$bottleneck))
frontiers$tolerance <- factor(frontiers$tolerance, levels = c("pi = 1.00", "pi = 0.95"))
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = d, aes(X, Y), size = 0.7, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_path(data = frontiers, aes(X_required, outcome_level, linetype = tolerance),
            colour = "grey10") +
  annotate("point", x = 2, y = 95, shape = 17, size = 2.5, colour = "grey10") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Condition X", y = "Outcome Y", linetype = NULL)
```

## The pointwise path

The summary counts the targets with a positive pointwise gap at the tolerances 0.95 and 0.90 and reports the largest gap and the target of the largest gap.

```{r tolerance-path-pointwise}
gap_rows <- function(data, label) {
  strict <- qnca(data$X, data$Y, pi = 1, B = 0, scope = scope)$bottleneck
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.95, 0.90), function(p) {
    b <- qnca(data$X, data$Y, pi = p, B = 0, scope = scope)$bottleneck
    data.frame(sample = label, tolerance = sprintf("pi = %.2f", p),
               target = b$outcome_level, gap = b$X_required - strict$X_required)
  }))
}
pointwise <- rbind(gap_rows(d, "clean sample"), gap_rows(planted, "planted sample"))
pointwise$tolerance <- factor(pointwise$tolerance, levels = c("pi = 0.95", "pi = 0.90"))
summary_gap <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(pointwise, ~ tolerance + sample), function(g) {
  data.frame(sample = g$sample[1], tolerance = g$tolerance[1],
             positive_targets = sum(g$gap > 0), max_gap = round(max(g$gap), 1),
             at_target = round(g$target[which.max(g$gap)], 1))
}))
rownames(summary_gap) <- NULL
summary_gap
```

At `pi = 0.95`, the clean sample has a positive gap at 34 of the 50 targets, with a largest gap of 19.0 at the target 18.4. The planted sample has a positive gap at 47 targets, with a largest gap of 59.9 at the target 61.2, because the strict frontier falls to the planted case.

```{r tolerance-path-pointwise-figure, fig.asp = 0.45, fig.cap = "Pointwise gap between the fitted frontier at pi = 0.95 or 0.90 and the fitted frontier at pi = 1.00 at each of the 50 outcome targets, for the synthetic dataset of 500 cases (clean sample) and for the same data with one planted case at (2, 95) (planted sample), fixed scope [0, 100] x [0, 100]."}
ggplot(pointwise, aes(target, gap, linetype = tolerance)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey10") +
  facet_wrap(~ sample) +
  labs(x = "Outcome target", y = "Pointwise gap", linetype = NULL)
```

## The resistance bound on the planted sample

The check applies the proposition with $c = 1$ at the targets where the clean sample selects a rank above 1 at `pi = 0.95`.

```{r tolerance-path-resistance}
clean_res <- qnca_resolution(d$X, d$Y, pi = 0.95, scope = scope)
planted_res <- qnca_resolution(planted$X, planted$Y, pi = 0.95, scope = scope)
resolved <- which(clean_res$rank > 1)
bounds <- t(sapply(resolved, function(j) {
  x <- sort(d$X[d$Y >= clean_res$y[j]])
  h <- clean_res$rank[j]
  c(lower = x[h - 1], upper = x[h + 1])
}))
raw_planted <- planted_res$raw[resolved]
last <- max(clean_res$y[resolved])
upper_band <- planted_res$y > last & planted_res$y < 95
data.frame(resolved_targets = length(resolved), last_resolved = round(last, 2),
           within_bounds = all(raw_planted >= bounds[, "lower"] & raw_planted <= bounds[, "upper"]),
           raw_above_last = max(planted_res$raw[upper_band]),
           fitted_above_last = round(max(planted_res$fitted[upper_band]), 2))
```

At `pi = 0.95`, 34 targets of the clean sample are reached by more than 20 cases, the last at the target 67.35. At each of the 34 targets, the raw requirement of the planted sample lies between the original order statistics of rank $h_j - 1$ and $h_j + 1$, as the proposition states for one added case. Between the target 67.35 and the outcome 95 of the planted case, the raw requirement falls to the condition value 2 of the planted case, and the envelope holds the requirement of 61.87 reached at the target 67.35.

## Deletion and addition screens

The deletion screen `qnca_outliers()` with `k = 1` deletes each case in turn, recomputes `d_pi` at the tolerances 1.00, 0.95 and 0.90 on the fixed scope and flags a case whose deletion changes an effect size by at least one percent, in the manner of the NCA outlier screen [@Deja2026QNCA].

```{r tolerance-path-deletion}
columns <- c("cases", "flagged", "dif_rel_1", "dif_rel_0.95", "dif_rel_0.9")
screen <- qnca_outliers(planted$X, planted$Y, k = 1, scope = scope)
head(screen$table[, columns], 3)
clean_screen <- qnca_outliers(d$X, d$Y, k = 1, scope = scope)
head(clean_screen$table[, columns], 2)
```

On the planted sample, the planted case 501 heads the screen with relative changes of 5.84 at `pi = 1`, 0.161 at `pi = 0.95` and 0.047 at `pi = 0.90`. On the clean sample, the screen flags case 195, a draw of the generator, with a relative change of 0.011 at `pi = 1`.

Deletion and the tolerance path answer different questions: deletion asks whether a case belongs in the data, whereas the tolerance path keeps the case and reports how the estimator responds across tolerances fixed in advance [@Deja2026QNCA]. NCA guidance asks whether a ceiling case reflects error, another population or valid heterogeneity, and ties removal to evidence of error or of another population [@DulHauffBouncken2023].

The addition screen `qnca_sensitivity()` adds 0 to 5 copies of the planted case to the clean sample and reports the retained share of the clean effect size, the empirical breakdown curve of `d_pi`.

```{r tolerance-path-addition}
added <- qnca_sensitivity(d$X, d$Y, points = c(2, 95), counts = 0:5, scope = scope)
retention <- data.frame(added = added$counts, round(added$retention, 3))
names(retention)[-1] <- sprintf("pi_%.2f", added$pi)
retention
```

One added case leaves the strict member 0.146 of the clean effect size, and further copies keep the strict share at 0.146, because the first copy already sets the ceiling at every target the copies attain. The member at `pi = 0.95` retains 0.861 with one added case and 0.441 with five, and the member at `pi = 0.90` retains 0.955 and 0.703. The copies sit at the outcome 95, in the sparse top of the outcome range, where the resistance of the tolerant members weakens [@Deja2026QNCA].

```{r tolerance-path-breakdown, fig.cap = "Breakdown curves for the synthetic dataset of 500 cases: the share of the clean effect size d_pi retained after adding 0 to 5 cases at (2, 95), at the tolerances pi = 1.00, 0.95 and 0.90, fixed scope [0, 100] x [0, 100], grid of 50 outcome targets."}
curve <- data.frame(added = rep(added$counts, times = length(added$pi)),
                    tolerance = rep(sprintf("pi = %.2f", added$pi), each = length(added$counts)),
                    retention = as.vector(added$retention))
curve$tolerance <- factor(curve$tolerance, levels = sprintf("pi = %.2f", added$pi))
ggplot(curve, aes(added, retention, linetype = tolerance, shape = tolerance)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey20") +
  geom_point(colour = "grey20", size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Added cases at (2, 95)", y = "Share of the clean effect size",
       linetype = NULL, shape = NULL)
```

The file `outlier_diagnostic.csv` of the repository stores the planted-boundary example of @Deja2026QNCA, a sample of 300 cases with the same planted case.

```{r tolerance-path-stored}
read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarekDejaUJ/qnca/main/data/outlier_diagnostic.csv",
         check.names = FALSE)
```

In the stored example, the strict effect size falls from 0.457 to 0.065, the effect size at `pi = 0.95` moves from 0.516 to 0.451, and the gap widens from 0.058 to 0.386.

## Outlier-fragility and spuriousness

Outlier-fragility and spuriousness are different failure modes. Outlier-fragility means that one or a few efficient cases hold the estimated boundary, and the tolerance path diagnoses outlier-fragility. Spuriousness means that correlation, skewness or a sufficiency relation produces the empty zone, and a spurious empty zone moves all members of the path together, so a flat path is compatible with spuriousness [@Deja2026QNCA]. The permutation test and the dependence-matched reference band of the function `spuriousness_band()` address spuriousness, and the band is a proposed diagnostic with operating characteristics still to be established [@Deja2026QNCA].

## The same path in Python and Julia

The Python and Julia packages return the same effect sizes and the same breakdown curve.

```{python tolerance-path-python}
from urllib.request import urlopen
import numpy as np
from qnca import qnca, qnca_sensitivity

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarekDejaUJ/qnca/main/data/qnca_dataset_n500.csv"
X, Y = np.loadtxt(urlopen(url), delimiter=",", skiprows=1, unpack=True)
scope = (0.0, 100.0, 0.0, 100.0)
Xp, Yp = np.append(X, 2.0), np.append(Y, 95.0)
for pi in (1.0, 0.95, 0.90):
    clean = qnca(X, Y, pi=pi, B=None, scope=scope).d_pi
    with_case = qnca(Xp, Yp, pi=pi, B=None, scope=scope).d_pi
    print(pi, clean, with_case)
added = qnca_sensitivity(X, Y, points=(2.0, 95.0), counts=range(6), scope=scope)
print(np.round(added.retention, 3))
```

```{julia tolerance-path-julia}
using QuantileNecessity, Downloads, DelimitedFiles

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarekDejaUJ/qnca/main/data/qnca_dataset_n500.csv"
data = readdlm(Downloads.download(url), ',', Float64; skipstart = 1)
X, Y = data[:, 1], data[:, 2]
scope = (0.0, 100.0, 0.0, 100.0)
Xp, Yp = vcat(X, 2.0), vcat(Y, 95.0)
for p in (1.0, 0.95, 0.90)
    clean = qnca(X, Y; pi = p, B = 0, scope = scope).d_pi
    with_case = qnca(Xp, Yp; pi = p, B = 0, scope = scope).d_pi
    println(p, " ", clean, " ", with_case)
end
added = qnca_sensitivity(X, Y; points = (2.0, 95.0), counts = 0:5, scope = scope)
foreach(println, eachrow(round.(added.retention; digits = 3)))
```
